title: Procore to acquire DroneDeploy for $845M
excerpt: The move will combine Procore’s hundreds of millions of drawings and photos with DroneDeploy’s 20 trillion square feet of visual data.
content_html:
Matthew Thibault

Thu, July 30, 2026 at 9:38 AM MST 2 min read

This story was originally published on Construction Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Construction Dive newsletter.

Dive Brief:

  • Contech giant Procore has entered an agreement to acquire DroneDeploy, a prominent robotics and visual intelligence platform that's used in over 180 countries, according to a Wednesday announcement. Procore will acquire the firm for $845 million in cash, subject to customary purchase price adjustments.

  • When the acquisition closes later this year, Procore and DroneDeploy will sell one another's solutions to their client base, Ajei Gopal, president and CEO of Procore, said in the announcement.

  • The combination will create a veritable ocean of construction data. By pairing the two tech companies' capabilities, builders will be able to use cameras, drones and robots to regularly evaluate jobsites and automatically initiate appropriate responses securely, compliantly and in context, per the announcement.

Dive Insight:

The deal underscores the power of data control in a landscape dominated by artificial intelligence. Simply put, data is king.

Procore's dataset includes nearly 400 million photos, more than 126 million drawings and over 10 million requests for information, submittals and inspections recorded on its platform in the last year alone, according to the firm. 

Meanwhile, DroneDeploy offers its visual record of physical builds, which spans approximately 20 trillion square feet of visual data for the built world, tens of millions of user-generated annotations and more than 100,000 labeled safety issues, per the announcement.

"For the longer term, adding DroneDeploy's technology into the Procore platform will enable us to accelerate our AI strategy and deliver digital coworkers that track what's happening on a project, make sense of it, and then take action to change the outcome," Gopal said in the announcement.

DroneDeploy is not alone as a Procore acquisition target. In January, it acquired Datagrid, a vertical AI firm that offers builders a host of AI agents. At the time, Procore flagged the acquisition as part of its strategy to bolster its AI strategy and capabilities. That maps out to the company's current stance, said Meg Baldini, vice president of corporate development & partnerships at Procore.

"We've always viewed acquisitions as a way to accelerate our strategy—they're never the strategy itself," Baldini told Construction Dive via email. "M&A is simply one tool we use to move faster, and both Datagrid and DroneDeploy are examples of acquisitions that strengthen our platform and accelerate our AI strategy."

这个故事最初发表在《Construction Dive》上。 要接收每日新闻和见解，请订阅我们免费的每日建筑潜水时事通讯。

潜水简介：

  • 根据周三的公告，Contech 巨头 Procore 已达成协议，收购 DroneDeploy，这是一个在 180 多个国家/地区使用的著名机器人和视觉智能平台。 Procore 将以 8.45 亿美元现金收购该公司，具体收购价格将根据惯例进行调整。
  • Procore 总裁兼首席执行官 Ajei Gopal 在公告中表示，今年晚些时候收购完成后，Procore 和 DroneDeploy 将向各自的客户群出售对方的解决方案。
  • 这种结合将创造出名副其实的建筑数据海洋。 根据公告，通过结合两家科技公司的能力，建筑商将能够使用摄像头、无人机和机器人定期评估工地，并根据具体情况安全、合规地自动启动适当的响应。

潜水洞察力：

这笔交易强调了在人工智能主导的环境中数据控制的力量。 简而言之，数据为王。

据该公司称，仅去年一年，Procore 的数据集就包括其平台上记录的近 4 亿张照片、超过 1.26 亿张图纸以及超过 1000 万条信息请求、提交和检查请求。

与此同时，根据公告，DroneDeploy 提供物理建筑的视觉记录，涵盖建筑世界约 20 万亿平方英尺的视觉数据、数千万个用户生成的注释和超过 100,000 个标记的安全问题。

Gopal 在声明中表示：“从长远来看，将 DroneDeploy 的技术添加到 Procore 平台将使我们能够加速我们的人工智能战略，并提供数字化同事来跟踪项目中发生的情况，理解项目，然后采取行动改变结果。”

DroneDeploy 并不是唯一一个成为 Procore 收购目标的公司。 一月份，它收购了 Datagrid，这是一家垂直人工智能公司，为建筑商提供大量人工智能代理。 当时，Procore 将此次收购视为其加强人工智能战略和能力战略的一部分。 Procore 企业发展与合作伙伴关系副总裁梅格·巴尔迪尼 (Meg Baldini) 表示，这符合该公司目前的立场。

“我们一直将收购视为加速我们战略的一种方式——它们从来都不是战略本身，”巴尔迪尼通过电子邮件告诉《Construction Dive》。 “并购只是我们用来加快步伐的一种工具，Datagrid 和 DroneDeploy 都是收购的例子，它们增强了我们的平台并加速了我们的人工智能战略。”
